sections.assessment: Budiarto, Purwanto, Halimatussadiah and Maharsi; Carbon Neutrality4:20(2025), DOI10.1007/s43979-025-00135-w. CC-BY4.0 statement inspected. Abstract reports~34% transport-cost reduction and annual-well-constrained network optimisation, not a full lifecycle benefit.

Read historical emissions/CCS statistics, hard-to-abate-sector arguments, MILP/MINLP/pinch/superstructure comparisons and limitations alleged for earlier injection timing/rate models. All58 bibliography identities and their roles are mapped below. General necessity/novelty and source criticisms remain attributed claims until those originals are checked.

South Sumatra has14 model sources,5.33MTPA rounded; eastern sources reportedly55% and northern/southwestern storage78%. Sources include combustion and AGRU streams, with gas-processing and ammonia emissions attributed torefs47/46. Current-producing reservoirs become available after forecast abandonment. These are modelled prospects, not allocated Japanese storage service.

14sources,2hubs,2junctions,8sinks. Hubs use existing gathering/logistics locations; junctions reference pipeline corridors. Direct hub-to-reservoir and hub-to-junction-to-reservoir routes are considered. Complete admissible arcs, junction–reservoir segment lengths and design-dependent costs are not enumerated by the supplied hub-distance table.

Separate capture, pipeline and well simulations generate parameters for a30-year network optimisation. Figure3 shows one-way parameter transfer; no code or fully coupled reservoir feedback implementation is retained.

HYSYSV11 MDEA/PZ capture, minimum90% target, Acid Gas–Chemical Solvents package;98.8wt% TEG dehydration. AGRU/ammonia streams receive dehydration only. Compression, solvent circulation and heat duties reportedly inform fixed capture costs, but no complete stream/heat/electricity inventory is supplied here.

Liquid/supercritical transport;13–44°C,85–150bar; HYSYSV11 Peng–Robinson calculations. Single-source diameters4–10in; hub-node14–22in. Purity, roughness and segment inlet conditions are named input classes but not provided as a complete case.

Python/PuLP/CBC stated. Cost objective includes capture,4route categories and injection/storage.2023USD;8% interest;30-year capture life; fixed and variableO&M each3%CAPEX. Annualised pipeline/storage costs depend on reservoir availability. Binary domains/activation equations, complete coefficients and solve tolerances are absent from the published formulation.

DCA for oil andp/z for gas abandonment forecasts; IPM-PROSPER compositionalEoS/JonesIPR injectivity. Wellhead limits50bar(gas),87bar(liquid); reservoir pressure≤90% estimated fracture pressure. Annualkr,t is said to aggregate allowable simulated injection. Pressure/efficiency plots and readiness/resource/cost table do not provide a complete calendar-timekr,t array or well model.

2027–2056 annual bins. SW-A single wells; MW-A adds wells to low-injectivityr1/r7/r8; MW-D delaysh1 until2039. Four wells are stated added tor1 andr7,twotor8(p12). All scenario maps, endpoint masses, annual hub-share plots and supplementary allocations inspected. Exact annual source flows and backlog/curtailment treatment remain unspecified.

Storage153.21Mt(SW-A) versus159.81Mt(MW-A/D). SW-A$17.53billion; multiwell total ranges differ by passage. Transport17.71/16.56/15.89USD/t. Figure11 full-chain and component averages and aggregate cost/mass ratios need common-basis reconciliation, not a forced corrected number.

MW-D full-storage enforcement; captureCAPEX+30%→fullcost+13.6%; transport+30%→+4.2%; uniform storage+30%→+0.7%; selectedr1/r6storage+50%→+0.6% and allocation shift. Under fixed captured volumes, capture-cost changes add an objective constant; unchanged network in that test is structurally expected.

IndonesianMEMR2/2023, Gundih public-engagement evidence and continuing local oil/gas employment are discussed. Proposed transfer to onshore pipeline networks of<300km radius is a modelling scope claim, not empirical validation of every geography or shipping chain.

Homogeneous reservoirs, literature/process-simulation parameters, fixed8% interest, existing infrastructure; heterogeneity, terrain, future expansion and regulatory influences not explicitly modelled. Read as author limitations rather than resolved uncertainties.

Conclusion restates153.21/159.81Mt, cost and34% transport results. All sets/mass/cost/kr,t/readiness symbols read. Data available from corresponding author on reasonable request; not a public code/data archive. Supplement notice, funding, contributions, declarations and received/revised/accepted/published dates inspected. No author contact sent.

All58 printed entries read, including entries23–26 and44–47 missed in one native-text view. Bibliographic originals remain unverified. Exact retained matches exist forSimCCS(B3-44) andZhang/Lau2022(B4-08). The retained Fraga2024(B2-12) is not silently substituted for the citedFraga2021 conference paper.

issues.finding: The seven supplemental pressure/efficiency curves and main r3 curve lack the calendar, pressure and state trajectories needed for all 240 reservoir-year kr,t inputs.
issues.action: Obtain annual bounds and well models with their state basis. Do not use optimised mr,t allocations as independent kr,t.

issues.finding: The printed formulation omits explicit binary/linking domains, a cumulative-resource constraint and full arc/activation-cost data. Table1 has five rows; reservoir inflow equality is described in prose.
